items.situation: Describe your favorite restaurant in one sentence.
A visitor asks: What is Bixiga? Answer in one sentence.
Describe a building you designed or love, with which.
Tell me about a city where people are very welcoming.
You have just described your neighborhood. Turn the question around.

listenings.text: Welcome to the Central Market. Before we buy anything, let me introduce you to the people, because they are the reason this market is special. The woman at the first stall is Marta. She is the woman who sells honey, and she has been here for forty years. Ask her about her bees. She will talk for an hour. The man with the white hat is a cheesemaker who comes down from the mountains every Friday, only Friday, so today you are lucky. And the young couple at the end are newcomers. They opened a stall which sells bread from old Slovenian recipes, and the regulars already love it. After shopping, the regulars all go to the small cafe under the arches, where everybody knows their order. Shall we?

This is the street where I grew up. When I was a boy, there was a shoemaker, a barber and a bakery here, run by families who lived above their shops. You knew everybody, and everybody knew you, and your mother. Fifty years later, the buildings are the same. The facades are beautiful, and somebody restored them very well. But the people are different. The old bakery is now a coffee shop which sells very expensive coffee, to people who stay for one year and then leave. I am not angry about it. Cities change. But there is one person who is still here. The barber, who is ninety years old, still cuts hair on Saturdays, in the same chair. I go every month, and I always ask for the same thing.

extra_audio.text: First Ricardo took Maja to Bixiga, the neighborhood where the Italian families arrived. Then they stopped at the bakery which opened in 1897. After that he showed her the street vendor who sells the best corn in the city. Then Maja asked if the people there were welcoming. In the end they talked about the places where they go on Sundays.
